key_insight: Adaptive variational quantum chemistry can get trapped by the qubit mapping itself: asymmetric geometries combined with Bravyi-Kitaev encoding create flat optimization landscapes, while symmetric point-group structure helps preserve trainability.
engineering_relevance: For practical quantum software and early fault-tolerant execution, ansatz design alone is not enough—fermion-to-qubit representation, symmetry handling, and runtime resource control must be co-designed to avoid wasted optimization effort.
method: Tested a spin-conserved SUSD operator pool on stretched LiH, BeH2, and H2O at 2×Re.
Compared asymmetric distortions against symmetric BeH2 to isolate symmetry-protection effects on the optimization landscape.
Added a covariance-driven adaptive shot-allocation filter that monitors gradient precision and stops circuits when gradients flatten.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic evaluation across multiple stretched molecules, showing representation-locked optimization trapping under asymmetric geometries and improved trainability when point-group symmetry is preserved.
watch_item: The covariance-based pruning/termination logic may be sensitive to noisy gradients and could prematurely stop useful circuits if the precision threshold is not carefully tuned.
paper_title: Representation-Induced Symmetry Trapping in Adaptive Variational Quantum Simulations of Multi-Reference Topologies
